title: Private Deployment Console — Cluster & Network Status, Upgrade Flows, and Cost Drilldowns
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a cohesive UX for Private/VPC deployments focused on three clustered experiences: 1) Cluster & network status surface (health, topology mini-map, alerts), 2) Upgrade and rollout flows (canary/staged upgrades, rollback actions, scheduling), and 3) Per-cluster cost and token usage drilldowns. The goal is a single workspace in Redwood Console where platform engineers can monitor health, run upgrades with confidence, and understand cost drivers at cluster and node pool granularity.
acceptance_criteria: Status dashboard shows per-cluster health, last-updated time, active incidents, and a compact topology mini-map for VPC subnets and nodes
Upgrade flow supports: create upgrade plan, select canary % and node pools, schedule window, dry-run validation, and single-click rollback from rollout history
Cost view exposes: token usage by model per-cluster, CPU/GPU hours, and anomaly flags with ability to link to request traces
Design prototypes reviewed and approved by PM and Eng for accessibility (contrast >= 4.5:1) and responsive behavior down to 1280px width
Handoff artifacts include Figma frames, component spec sheet, HTML/CSS token guidance, and a prioritized engineering backlog with tickets
Usability test (n=6 platform engineers) shows at least 80% success rate for initiating a staged upgrade and finding the cost-hotspot for the past 7 days
design_notes: Primary surface is a workspace tab under each Private deployment: Overview / Status / Upgrades / Cost / Logs
Status header uses a compact ‘health ribbon’ (green/yellow/red) with hover cards for immediate context (active alerts, incidents, SLOs impacted)
Topology mini-map is an interactive SVG with selectable node pools and subnet overlays; clicking a node opens side-panel with metrics and recent traces
Upgrade modal uses progressive disclosure: basic quick-upgrade for 1-click patching, and advanced plan builder for canary percents, node pool selection, and post-upgrade smoke tests
Rollout timeline visualizes per-node rollout and allows lateral rollback to a specific step. Keep operations visible but require confirmation and audit-log entry for rollback actions
Cost drilldown uses a stacked bar per day with toggles for model, token type (input/output), and infra costs. Anomaly markers show % change vs baseline and link to sample requests
Design uses existing console tokens but extends signage colors for ‘maintenance window’ and ‘upgrade in progress’ states
Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation for timeline and modal; ARIA live regions for status updates during rollouts
decisions: Chosen single-page workspace per deployment rather than separate micro-pages to reduce context switching
Topology mini-map will render simplified network layout (logical grouping) to avoid revealing customer IPs—sensitive details behind permissioned side-panel
Default upgrade behavior will be conservative: 10% canary on first rollout unless PTO-enabled policy overrides
Cost view will surface precomputed summaries from backend pipeline; expensive ad-hoc queries will be gated behind 'refresh' button to avoid accidental load
tradeoffs: Information density vs clarity: decided to hide low-priority metrics behind a 'metrics drawer' to keep the status surface scannable
Real-time updates can be chatty; use push for critical alerts and 30s polling for non-critical metrics to balance console perf
Topology fidelity vs PII: reduced fidelity to protect network addressing while keeping useful operator signals
